step_by_step_reasoning:
1. Identified core architecture nodes based on visual layout and transcript: SQS, Lambda, DynamoDB, Step Functions, Neptune, Gremlin (ThirdParty), S3, and Glue.
2. Verified service types against valid vocabulary list (e.g. Gremlin maps to ThirdParty, Step Functions maps to StepFunctions, Dynamo DB maps to DynamoDB).
3. Identified logical connections and flows: SQS triggers job initiator Lambda -> Lambda reads pipeline configuration/status from DynamoDB -> DynamoDB feeds parameters into Step Functions -> Step Functions orchestrates loading data to Neptune and scaling instances -> Gremlin queries run against graph database and export results to S3 -> S3 data is cataloged by Glue.
4. Formatted all fields strictly matching JSON schema without raw control characters or forbidden services.

graph.name: HomeSite Insurance Graph Database and Data Pipeline Architecture
graph.notes: Architecture demonstrating serverless ingestion into Amazon Neptune graph database, managed with AWS Step Functions, DynamoDB, SQS, and exported to S3 for Glue cataloging.

nodes.name: SQS
nodes.notes: SQS queue receiving completion events from upstream serverless data pipelines.

nodes.name: LAMBDA

nodes.name: DYNAMO DB

nodes.name: NEPTUNE

nodes.name: GREMLIN

nodes.name: S3

nodes.name: GLUE

edges.notes: SQS queue natively triggers execution of the job initiator Lambda function.
Lambda function reads pipeline definitions and status records from DynamoDB.
Pipeline state and configuration from DynamoDB feed parameters into Step Functions execution.
Step Functions scales up Neptune cluster instances via Boto3 and loads vertices and edges.
Gremlin queries traverse the graph model and export results directly to S3.
AWS Glue catalogs exported dataset files stored in S3.
